answer: Skeptical by default: staked peer review only means something when the panel is diverse enough that collusion is expensive. Panels of 5 must cover 3 subnets and 2 client builds, 1 answer in 25 is re-run as a spot check, and a panel that fails diversity voids the whole batch, so the delta between paid and unpaid epochs becomes the attacker's real cost. Concrete case: two identities on one host reviewing each other get voided the moment the beacon assigns a third from outside, which is 4 panels in 5. An oasis of colluders looks fine until the void.
